37199-ecology-of-the-opossum-on-a-natura.title: in Northeastern Kansas
37199-ecology-of-the-opossum-on-a-natura.creator: Unknown
37199-ecology-of-the-opossum-on-a-natura.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The opossum plays an important part in this process of change; being relatively large, numerous, and of omnivorous habits, it variously influences, directly and indirectly, the populations of its plant and animal associates, through a complex web of interrelationships.

arxiv-2108-11355.title: FogROS: An Adaptive Framework for Automating Fog Robotics Deployment
arxiv-2108-11355.creator: Kaiyuan (Eric) Chen, Yafei Liang, Nikhil Jha, Jeffrey Ichnowski, Michael Danielczuk, Joseph Gonzalez, John Kubiatowicz, Ken Goldberg
arxiv-2108-11355.description: Abstract As many robot automation applications increasingly rely on multi-core processing or deep-learning models, cloud computing is becoming an attractive and economically viable resource for systems that do not contain high computing power onboard. Despite its immense computing capacity, it is often underused by the robotics and automation community due to lack of expertise in cloud computing and cloud-based infrastructure.

arxiv-2112-09966.title: An application of a moment problem to completely monotonic functions
arxiv-2112-09966.creator: Vladimir Jovanović 1, Milanka Treml 1
arxiv-2112-09966.description: Abstract . We consider the following question: if a function of the form ∫ 0 ∞ φ ⁡ ( t ) ​ e − x ​ t ​ 𝑑 t \int_{0}^{\infty}\varphi(t)\,e^{-xt}dt is completely monotonic, is it then φ ⩾ 0 \varphi\geqslant 0 ? It turns out that the question is related to a moment problem.

arxiv-2202-08305.title: Understanding viscoelastic flow instabilities: Oldroyd-B and beyond Note: Published in the Oldroyd-100 special issue of the Journal of non-Newtonian Fluid Mechanics
arxiv-2202-08305.creator: Hugo A. Castillo Sánchez, Mihailo R. Jovanović, Satish Kumar, Alexander Morozov, V. Shankar, Ganesh Subramanian, Helen J. Wilson
arxiv-2202-08305.description: Abstract The Oldroyd-B model has been used extensively to predict a host of instabilities in shearing flows of viscoelastic fluids, often realized experimentally using polymer solutions. The present review, written on the occasion of the birth centenary of James Oldroyd, provides an overview of instabilities found across major classes of shearing flows.

arxiv-2208-07636.title: Schwinger, ltd: Loop-tree duality in the parametric representation
arxiv-2208-07636.creator: Marko Berghoff
arxiv-2208-07636.description: Abstract . We derive a variant of the loop-tree duality for Feynman integrals in the Schwinger parametric representation. This is achieved by decomposing the integration domain into a disjoint union of cells, one for each spanning tree of the graph under consideration. Each of these cells is the total space of a fiber bundle with contractible fibers over a cube.

arxiv-2209-01774.title: ElasticROS: An Elastically Collaborative Robot Operation System for Fog and Cloud Robotics Manuscript received June 1, 2022; revised August 26, 2022; accept August 26, 2022. Boyi Liu, Lujia Wang are with Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. email: bl
arxiv-2209-01774.creator: Boyi Liu
arxiv-2209-01774.description: Abstract Robots are integrating more huge-size models to enrich functions and improve accuracy, which leads to out-of-control computing pressure. And thus robots are encountering bottlenecks in computing power and battery capacity. Fog or cloud robotics is one of the most anticipated theories to address these issues. Approaches of cloud robotics have developed from system-level to node-level.

arxiv-2305-02532.title: Compound WKI-SP hierarchy and multiloop soliton solutions Journal: XXX
arxiv-2305-02532.creator: Xiaorui Hu, Tianle Xu, Junyang Zhang, Shoufeng Shen
arxiv-2305-02532.description: Abstract The generalized hierarchies of compound WKI-SP (Wadati-Konno-Ichikawa and short pulse) equations are presented. The proposed integrable nonlinear equations include the WKI-type equations, the SP-type equations and the compound generalized WKI-SP equations. A chain of hodograph transformations are established to relate the compound WKI-SP equations with the MKdV-SG (modified Korteweg-de Vries and sine-Gordon) equations.

arxiv-2306-16417.title: On the Jacobson radical and semisimplicity of a semiring
arxiv-2306-16417.creator: A. K. Bhuniya, Puja Sarkar
arxiv-2306-16417.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A. K. Bhuniya, Puja Sarkar. Based on the minimal and simple representations, we introduce two Jacobson-type Hoehnke radicals, m-radical and s-radical, of a semiring S S . Every minimal (simple) S S -semimodule is a quotient of S S by a regular right congruence (maximal) μ \mu on S S such that [ 0 ] μ [0]_{\mu} is a maximal μ \mu -saturated right ideal in S S . Thus the m(s)-radical becomes an intersection of some regular congruences.

arxiv-2404-07933.title: Boosting Self-Supervision for Single-View Scene Completion via Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2404-07933.creator: Keonhee Han, Dominik Muhle, Felix Wimbauer, Daniel Cremers
arxiv-2404-07933.description: Abstract Inferring scene geometry from images via Structure from Motion is a long-standing and fundamental problem in computer vision. While classical approaches and, more recently, depth map predictions only focus on the visible parts of a scene, the task of scene completion aims to reason about geometry even in occluded regions.

arxiv-2501-14036.title: Efficient Precision Control in Object Detection Models for Enhanced and Reliable Ovarian Follicle Counting
arxiv-2501-14036.creator: Vincent Blot, Alexandra Lorenzo de Brionne, Ines Sellami, Olivier Trassard, Isabelle Beau, Charlotte Sonigo, Nicolas J.-B. Brunel
arxiv-2501-14036.description: Abstract Image analysis is a key tool for describing the detailed mechanisms of folliculogenesis, such as evaluating the quantity of mouse Primordial ovarian Follicles (PMF) in the ovarian reserve. The development of high-resolution virtual slide scanners offers the possibility of quantifying, robustifying and accelerating the histopathological procedure.

arxiv-2503-21081.title: Leveraging External Controls in Clinical Trials: Estimands, Estimation, Assumptions Volume: XX
arxiv-2503-21081.creator: Bo Liu 1,∗, Laine Thomas 2,∗∗, Rury R. Holman 3,∗∗∗, Fan Li 1,∗∗∗∗ 1 Department of Statistical Science, Duke University, Durham, North Carolina 27708, U.S.A. 2 Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Duke University, Durham, North Carolina 27708, U.S.A 3 Radcliffe Department of Medicine, Oxf
arxiv-2503-21081.description: Abstract It is increasingly common to augment randomized controlled trial with external controls from observational data, to evaluate the treatment effect of an intervention. Traditional approaches to treatment effect estimation involve ambiguous estimands and unrealistic or strong assumptions, such as mean exchangeability.

plos-pone-0000622.creator: Rudi Alberts, Peter Terpstra, Yang Li et al.
plos-pone-0000622.description: PLOS ONE research article. Many investigations have reported the successful mapping of quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for gene expression phenotypes (eQTLs). Local eQTLs, where expression phenotypes map to the genes themselves, are of especially great interest, because they are direct candidates for previo

plos-pone-0003173.title: Rapid Molecular Detection of Rifampicin Resistance Facilitates Early Diagnosis and Treatment of Multi-Drug Resistant Tuberculosis: Case Control Study
plos-pone-0003173.creator: Philly O'Riordan, Uli Schwab, Sarah Logan et al.
plos-pone-0003173.description: PLOS ONE research article. Multi-drug resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is a major public health concern since diagnosis is often delayed, increasing the risk of spread to the community and health care workers. Treatment is prolonged, and the total cost of treating a single case is high. Diagnosis has tradit

pmc-10558974.title: Virtual tumor boards: An approach to equity in cancer care
pmc-10558974.creator: Mina AkbariRad, Sareh Keshvardoost, Hanie Shariatmadari, Abdollah Firoozi, AmirAli Moodi Ghalibaf
pmc-10558974.description: gap between developed and non-developed countries.1 A multidisciplinary approach involving oncologists, radiotherapists, surgeons, and pathologists is crucial for optimal cancer management and treatment decision-making. Tumor board meetings, where experts convene to discuss treatment options, have proven instrumental in achieving accurate diagnoses, informed treatment choices, and improved patient outcomes.

pmc-11355398.title: The Catalase Gene MrCat1 Contributes to Oxidative Stress Tolerance, Microsclerotia Formation, and Virulence in the Entomopathogenic Fungus Metarhizium rileyi
pmc-11355398.creator: Yu Su, Xuyi Wang, Yuanli Luo, Huan Jiang, Guiting Tang, Huai Liu, Jiaqin Xie, Nicolás Pedrini
pmc-11355398.description: Catalases play a crucial role in the metabolism of reactive oxygen species (ROS) by converting H2O2 into molecular oxygen and water. They also contribute to virulence and fungal responses to various stresses. Previously, the MrCat1-deletion mutant (ΔMrCat1) was generated using the split-marker method in Metarhizium rileyi. In this study, the Cat1 gene was identified, and its function was evaluated.

pmc-11484623.title: The use of plasma exchange with albumin replacement in the management of Alzheimer’s disease: a scoping review
pmc-11484623.creator: Yahveth Cantero-Fortiz, Mercè Boada
pmc-11484623.description: IntroductionAD is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder causing significant cognitive decline and impaired daily functioning. Current treatments offer only modest relief, and many amyloid-targeting therapies have failed, prompting exploration of alternative approaches such as PE with albumin replacement.ObjectivesThis scoping review systematically maps the literature on PE with albumin replacement in AD management, focusing on outcomes, methodologies, and reported benefits and risks.

pmc-11548448.title: Isotopic and Geophysical Investigations of Groundwater in Laiyuan Basin, China
pmc-11548448.creator: Weiqiang Wang, Zilong Meng, Chenglong Wang, Jianye Gui
pmc-11548448.description: Due to the complex intersection and control of multiple structural systems, the hydrogeological conditions of the Laiyuan Basin in China are complex. The depth of research on the relationship between geological structure and groundwater migration needs to be improved. The supply relationship of each aquifer is still uncertain.

pmc-11643758.title: A Comprehensive Review on Dietary Polysaccharides as Prebiotics, Synbiotics, and Postbiotics in Infant Formula and Their Influences on Gut Microbiota
pmc-11643758.creator: Wenyuan Zhang, Yanli Zhang, Yaqi Zhao, Liang Li, Zhanquan Zhang, Kasper Hettinga, Haixia Yang, Jianjun Deng, Miguel Romero-Pérez
pmc-11643758.description: Human milk contains an abundance of nutrients which benefit the development and growth of infants. However, infant formula has to be used when breastfeeding is not possible. The large differences between human milk and infant formula in prebiotics lead to the suboptimal intestinal health of infant formula-fed infants.

pmc-12504685.title: SLC25A10 promotes cisplatin resistance by inhibiting ferroptosis in cervical cancer
pmc-12504685.creator: Chenglei Ma, Xiaoyi Lu, Chen Ni, Yu Gao, Fei Yang, Shiwen Chen, Yi Du, Fang Zhao, Ying Cao, Haiwei Huang
pmc-12504685.description: Cisplatin (DDP)-based chemotherapy is the standard first-line treatment for cervical cancer (CC). However, many patients with CC develop resistance to DDP, either initially or over time. This resistance significantly limits the effectiveness of treatment. Therefore, identifying new therapeutic targets and combination therapies to overcome DDP resistance is a critical need.

pmc-12553069.title: TRPV6-mediated Store-operated Ca2+ Entry Participates in Pancreatic Acinar Cell Injury During Acute Pancreatitis
pmc-12553069.creator: Chenxia Han, Yuncheng Luo, Zhenlu Li, Lu Li, Jiawang Li, Ping Liao, Li Li, Juan Lin, Shiyu Liu, Tingting Liu, Dan Du, Wei Huang, Ruotian Jiang, Qing Xia
pmc-12553069.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background & AimsSuppressing toxic Ca2+ accumulation in pancreatic acinar cells (PACs) is the central therapeutic strategy of acute pancreatitis (AP). Store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) represents an important mechanism promoting Ca2+ overload, which remains incompletely understood in AP. Transient receptor potential vanilloid 6 (TRPV6) is an ion channel highly selective to Ca2+, and its role in PACs or AP onset remains largely unknown.MethodsWe utilized human and mouse pancreata for TRPV6 expression using RNAscope and PACs for electrophysical currents and Ca2+ signals identification.

pmc-12568100.title: Multi-Sensor Data Fusion and Vibro-Acoustic Feature Engineering for Health Monitoring and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Hydraulic Valves
pmc-12568100.creator: Xiaomin Li, Liming Zhang, Tian Tan, Xiaolong Wang, Xinwen Zhao, Yanlong Xu, Andrea Cataldo
pmc-12568100.description: The reliability of hydraulic valves is critical for the safety and efficiency of industrial systems. While vibration and pressure sensors are widely deployed for condition monitoring, leveraging the heterogeneous data from these multi-sensor systems for accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction remains challenging due to noise, outliers, and inconsistent sampling rates.

pmc-12717467.title: Field Evidence of Endogenous Vitamin D Synthesis in Atlantic Salmon Induced by Natural Sunlight
pmc-12717467.creator: Christina Aspaas Husebø, Kjetil Berge, Frederike Keitel-Gröner, Eirik Hoel, Johan Rennemo, Margunn Sandstad, Kristine Marie Bjerkestrand, Lukas Lorentzen, Eirik Welde, Thea Morken, Ingunn Stubhaug, Julia Mullins, Håvard Bjørgen, Thea Bossum, Cato Brede, David Lausten Knudsen, Ikram Belghit
pmc-12717467.description: Fish are believed not to synthesize vitamin D through UV exposure but to meet their requirements from dietary sources. The high vitamin D levels found in many fish species are thought to originate from UV‐induced synthesis in plankton, with vitamin D subsequently accumulating through the aquatic food chain.

pmc-13184327.title: Fear learning in unmedicated patients with anxiety disorders: a comparison of delay conditioning, fear reversal, and trace conditioning
pmc-13184327.creator: Enric Vilajosana, Simone Battaglia, Pamela Chavarría-Elizondo, Ignacio Martínez‑Zalacaín, Asier Juaneda-Seguí, Cristina Saiz-Masvidal, Víctor De la Peña-Arteaga, Alexander J Shackman, Joaquim Radua, Carles Soriano-Mas, Miquel A Fullana
pmc-13184327.description: Anxiety disorders are common and impairing, yet their underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Fear learning provides a critical translational framework for investigating pathological anxiety, bridging laboratory models and clinical phenomena. Prior studies have been limited by important methodological issues, including the inclusion of non-anxiety diagnoses, high comorbidity, and medication use.

pmc-13261060.title: Factors influencing Purdue Pegboard test results among hand-arm vibration-exposed workers
pmc-13261060.creator: A Stjernbrandt, I Liljelind, H Pettersson
pmc-13261060.description: BackgroundManual dexterity can be assessed using the Purdue Pegboard test (PPT) and used for staging of hand-arm vibration (HAV) syndrome.AimsTo describe PPT results among HAV-exposed workers and investigate what factors influence the results.MethodsWe recruited workers from companies and an occupational medicine clinic in Sweden. They responded to a survey, underwent neurosensory testing and completed the PPT.

pmc-13291449.title: Real-world outcomes of FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel and prognostic factors in advanced pancreatic cancer: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13291449.creator: Carlos Escriva-Aranda, Eduardo Giner-Moreno, Emilio Soria Hernández, Josep Esteve Gallego, Elisa Gómez Roch, Patricia Capdevila, Cristobal Carrasco Picazo, Alba Ortiz Gracia, Daniel Vidal Jiménez, Jorge Aparicio, Robert Díaz Beveridge

pmc-13470015.title: How ecocentric leadership drives environmental performance through green culture and work engagement in Egyptian hospitality and tourism
pmc-13470015.creator: Mohammed Aldoghan, Hanan Eid Badwy, Nadia A Abdelmegeed Abdelwahed, Bassam Samir Al-Romeedy
pmc-13470015.description: This study investigates the impact of ecocentric leadership on environmental performance in the Egyptian hospitality and tourism sector. It explores the mediating roles of green organizational learning, as well as the sequential mediation of digital green culture and green work engagement, grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Social Exchange Theory (SET).

pmc-13516957.title: Luminescent Imaging of the Reverse Bias Behavior of Perovskite Solar Cells Using ReBEL
pmc-13516957.creator: Jonathan Henzel, Klaas Bakker, Sjoerd Veenstra, Olindo Isabella, Luana Mazzarella, Arthur Weeber, Mirjam Theelen
pmc-13516957.description: Partial shading remains a critical challenge for perovskite photovoltaics, as shaded cells in otherwise illuminated modules operate in reverse bias, which can accelerate degradation. In other solar cell technologies, reverse bias electroluminescence (ReBEL) imaging has been successfully employed to investigate the reverse bias breakdown mechanism.

pmc-13688731.title: Does a mobile interactive web application improve dental students’ panoramic radiograph interpretation skills? A pre–post educational study
pmc-13688731.creator: Beyza Yalvaç Pınarbaşı, Kemal Selçuk Yücel, Deniz Ezgi Şakalakoğlu, Emin Murat Canger
pmc-13688731.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThis study aims to evaluate the impact of a newly developed, mobile-compatible web application on the learning process of dental interns, specifically focusing on its effectiveness in the interpretation of panoramic radiographs.MethodsThe study included 60 third-year dental students. For educational purposes, a total of 61 anatomical regions and landmarks in both jaws, 20 intraosseous pathologies, and 26 dental materials with distinct radiographic appearances were identified.
